items.title: A derived complete module whose reduction modulo the ideal is finite is the completion of a finite module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal of a Noetherian ring A and M a derived complete A-module. The lemma asserts that if M/IM is a finite A/I-module then M = lim M/I^nM and M is a finite A^wedge-module (source lines 27291-27297). The proof picks x_1, ..., x_t in M mapping to generators of M/IM and obtains a map A^{oplus t} -> M sending the i-th basis vector to x_i (proof lines 27300-27302). By the Noetherian proposition on naive completion, the derived completion of A is A^wedge = lim A/I^n (proof lines 27302-27305). Because M is derived complete, the map factors through a map q : (A^wedge)^{oplus t} -> M (proof lines 27305-27306). The cokernel Coker(q) is zero by the statement that a derived complete module annihilated by I is zero (proof lines 27307-27308), so M is a finite A^wedge-module (proof line 27309). Finally, since A^wedge is Noetherian and complete with respect to IA^wedge, it follows that M is I-adically complete, quoting three results from the Algebra chapter on completion of Noetherian rings, finite modules over complete rings and Artin-Rees (proof lines 27310-27314). The non-routine content is the factorization of the generator map through the completion, which is what converts a statement about M/IM into a statement about finite generation over the completion.
